title: Per-observable 100× experimental accuracy status
html:
Remark. Per-observable 100× experimental accuracy status

Remark (per-observable 100\times experimental status).

The per-observable accuracy record is the witness computations/per-observable-100x-status.witness.json, emitted by per_observable_100x_status.py. It records, for each predicted observable, whether the prediction meets its 100\times absolute-accuracy target against experiment. Its summary field carries the headline counts. The accuracy result is beats_100x_scoreable out of scoreable_total, which count predictions only. beats_100x_count must not be quoted as an accuracy result: it also counts the calibration inputs the witness lists in summary.calibration_inputs, whose residuals are fixed by construction rather than measured. The remainder do not meet the target, and closing them is open.

Target. For each predicted observable O with experimental uncertainty \sigma_{\mathrm{exp}}(O), the 100\times target is \sigma_{\mathrm{pred}}(O) \leq \sigma_{\mathrm{exp}}(O) / 100.

Current status. Numbers are not inlined here, because they change as the predictions are sharpened; the authoritative values are the witness's per-row pred_err, 100x_target and beats_100x flags, together with the summary counts beats_100x_scoreable / scoreable_total. The witness is recomputed whenever its upstream inputs change — the per-observable comparison values are read from the production witness for each anchor — so it does not go stale silently.

Scope of the target. The 100\times target is one of two accuracy sub-goals, both measuring absolute accuracy against experiment. Both are distinct from the separate requirement of internal compute agreement, and both are bounded below by the CAL-2 calibration floor: no prediction can be sharper than the calibration it rests on.
